breaks.quote: If the honest answer is no, something good has to go.
breaks.why: The ask to prune rests on the author's one story and a few lines about the list, so a doubtful reader could shrug and keep everything.

breaks.quote: It hurts because you are pruning good things, and the good things are what fill the month.
breaks.why: The cost is named and the reader's strongest doubt (why cut good things, why not do each less) is never answered with a reason.

breaks.quote: And whatever you find you truly need, you can plant again later, from a fresh seed and with a clear mind.
breaks.why: The benefit is one sentence and the ask is squeezed into the last lines, so the reader is not convinced it is worth the cost.
